name: Edward Partridge
dateNote: He was baptized on 11 December 1830, named bishop in February 1831, and tarred and feathered in Independence in July 1833.
importance: Section 36 calls him to preach after his baptism in December 1830. Section 41 names him the first bishop, and section 42 gives the bishop his duties under the law of consecration. In Missouri he divided inheritances in Zion (57–58), though the revelations also call him to repent of disagreements with Joseph Smith. Joseph Smith addressed the Liberty Jail letters (121–123) to him and the Church.
connections: He married Lydia Clisbee and had lived in Painesville, Ohio, near Sidney Rigdon’s congregation. He worked alongside Sidney Gilbert and Newel K. Whitney, and section 124 counts him among the faithful dead.

sources.title: Edward Partridge, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 27 Aug. 1793, Pittsfield, Massachusetts; baptized by Joseph Smith 11 Dec. 1830; first bishop Feb. 1831; tarred and feathered July 1833; bishop in Clay and Caldwell Counties; bishop at Commerce 1839; died 27 May 1840, Nauvoo. “Edward” alone occurs once (36:1) for him.
